A.explanation: This uses $f = v/L = 450/1.35$, treating the 1.35 m length as one full wavelength instead of three half-wavelengths.

B.explanation: This does not follow from $L = 3\lambda/2$ and $f = v/\lambda$ with $L = 1.35 \text{ m}$ and $v = 450 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: With three loops, $L = 3\lambda/2$ gives $\lambda = 0.90 \text{ m}$, so $f = v/\lambda = 450/0.90 = 500 \text{ Hz}$.

D.explanation: This is twice the correct frequency, obtained by treating each loop as a full wavelength so $\lambda = 0.45 \text{ m}$.

Use the wave equation $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 450 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and your value of $\lambda$ to calculate $f$ in $\text{Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify the pattern from the diagram: the string is fixed with nodes at both ends and shows three complete loops between the 1.35 m marks.
State the stationary wave rule for fixed ends: length $L = n\lambda/2$, where $n$ is the number of half-wavelength loops. Here $n = 3$.
Calculate $\lambda = 2.70/3 = 0.90 \text{ m}$ and check the unit is metres.
Use $v = f\lambda$, rearranged to $f = v/\lambda$, with $v = 450 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute to get $f = 450/0.90 = 500 \text{ Hz}$. This is option C.
